m1_sort_stability.STATEMENT: making the splat sort a STABLE TOTAL ORDER (depth key tie-broken by splat index) makes cross-upload renders bit-identical
m1_sort_stability.diagnosis: the GPU bitonic compare-swap uses STRICT inequality on the depth key alone (sort.comp: swap only when keys[a] > keys[b] or keys[a] < keys[b]), so EQUAL depth keys never swap and the tie order entering each frame's sort is whatever the index buffer carried in -- and the index buffer is re-initialized only when the splat COUNT changes, never on re-upload of the same count. The converged tie arrangement therefore depends on upload history: the same buffer posted twice sorts ties differently on some frames.
m1_sort_stability.fix: the comparator becomes a total order: compare depth keys first, break ties by the splat INDEX carried in the permutation itself (indices are unique for real splats; padding entries all carry index 0 and key 0xFFFFFFFF and are indistinguishable, which is inert -- they always sort after every real key and their mutual order is byte-invisible). With (key,index) unique per real splat, the fully sorted permutation is UNIQUE, so the render no longer depends on the state entering the sort.
m1_sort_stability.PREDICTION: the same splat buffer posted via 4 SEPARATE uploads to the FIXED engine renders byte-identical PNG frames: all 24 frames of the 24-frame orbit are byte-equal across all 4 uploads
m1_sort_stability.FALSIFIER: any byte difference across uploads in any frame = RED, with the frame named and the differing-pixel count and max per-pixel delta reported (per-pixel max delta over RGB channels, computed exactly as the movie lane computed it: numpy int16 absolute difference of the decoded PNGs, max over channels, pixels_differing = count of pixels with delta > 0). Byte-equality with the PRE-FIX engine's outputs is NOT claimed and NOT required: the tie order changes by design; the falsifier pins cross-upload determinism of the NEW engine only.
m1_sort_stability.performance_claim: the sort must not regress measurably: same number of compare-swap stages and dispatches (the fix adds one uint comparison on key equality inside the existing shader); render time before/after reported for the identical orbit; a >2x slowdown is a finding

m2_argc_guard.STATEMENT: argument parsing that never dereferences beyond the true argc makes extra flags legal (or cleanly rejected with a message and exit code 1, never FAST_FAIL)
m2_argc_guard.diagnosis: main() reads argv[4] under an `argc > 3` guard (main.cpp: `int w = atoi(argv[3]), h = atoi(argv[4]);`); with argc == 4, argv[4] is nullptr and atoi(nullptr) aborts through ucrtbase!invoke_watson with FAST_FAIL_INVALID_ARG. `chimera_engine.exe 8097 --hidden --no-restore` is argc 4 and dies at startup.
m2_argc_guard.fix: a real argument parser at the top of main(): positionals (port, board file, legacy width/height) and value flags (--width/--height/--science-surface/--thermal-salvage/--earth-patch) are read only after an argc bound check; boolean flags (--hidden, --no-restore, --preserve-mesh-topology) are recognized anywhere; an UNKNOWN flag or a value flag missing its value is rejected with a one-line stderr usage message and exit code 1. No argv index >= argc is ever dereferenced.
m2_argc_guard.PREDICTION: launching with `--hidden --no-restore <port>` and with `<port>` alone both start the engine and serve frames; a deliberately bad arg (a flag expecting a value, given none, e.g. `--port`) exits with a clear stderr message and exit code 1
m2_argc_guard.FALSIFIER: any launch variant that crashes without a message = RED (the process dies by an abort/FAST_FAIL path -- observed as exit code 3 (FAST_FAIL / abort) or 0xC0000409-class termination with empty stderr -- instead of exiting 1 with the usage message)

m3_scorer_repair.STATEMENT: scoring discrimination on a POSTURE/ANATOMY token vocabulary (curated BEFORE measuring) separates the true mount from both probes where raw-text similarity could not
m3_scorer_repair.diagnosis: the movie lane's F1 scorer compared concatenated judgment TEXT through senses.align; boilerplate similarity (both reports describe 'a single isolated object on a black background') swamped the signal: align(true, trunk-rotated-90 deg probe) = 0.9 although every probe frame read says 'lying/horizontal, not upright'.
m3_scorer_repair.fix: an align_vocab(true_report, probe_report) instrument: each report is reduced to the set of vocabulary terms it hits (case-insensitive, word-boundary regex, from the banked vocabulary below); the score is the Jaccard of the two matched-term sets (|A and B| / |A or B|; 0.0 when both sets are empty -- no vocabulary evidence of alignment is a score of 0, never a NaN). Boilerplate contains no vocabulary terms and therefore cannot contribute.
m3_scorer_repair.PREDICTION: on the movie lane's OWN RECORDED verbatim judgments (the three judgement_*.json copied read-only from its validation dir into this one), vocab_align(true, P1) < 0.5 AND vocab_align(true, P2) < 0.5
m3_scorer_repair.FALSIFIER: either score >= 0.5 = RED. The vocabulary below was banked in this pre-registered block BEFORE the comparison ran; no term is added, removed or re-weighted after seeing a score.

instrument_details.scoring_rule: Jaccard over matched vocabulary term sets; 0.0 if both sides match nothing; the discrimination gate is the movie lane's own pre-registered 0.5 (a probe scoring >= 0.5 is NOT distinguished)
instrument_details.match_rule: word-boundary, case-insensitive substring for single words; multiword entries ('rib cage', 'non-solid') matched literally; 'radius' is ambiguous with a circle's radius but is banked as an anatomy term (the reports describe bones, not geometry) and stays as banked
instrument_details.categories_are_labels_only: the score uses the UNION of all matched terms as one set; the category labels exist to document provenance of each term, not to weight the score
